_comment: Labelled corpus for scripts/check-doc-citations.mjs (--selftest).
Every `line` is copied verbatim from a tracked file in this repo; `source` records where.
`tracked` is a synthetic tracked-file set, NOT live `git ls-files`, so an unrelated docs
rename cannot silently break the selftest.
`expect` lists the references the extractor must produce, in order, each with the
resolution rule that must accept it: exact | relative | docs, or null when unresolved.
Written before the regex, per the label-corpus-first rule in persistent-rules.md.
`allowlistCases` covers the other half of the checker: whether an allowlist entry still
earns its place. Each case pairs a synthetic allowlist with the set of references a scan
left unresolved, and states which entries should come back as no longer cited.
Both directions are measured, because a rule that only ever reports failures and a rule
that only ever reports success are indistinguishable from a single passing case.
`lineCases` covers the line-number ratchet. `lineTracked` is a second synthetic tracked-file
set, holding source paths rather than documents, so a classification case says which bucket a
cited path falls into: frozen when exactly one tracked file can be meant, ambiguous when two or
more carry the name, unresolved when none does. Negative cases state what must NOT read as a
position, because a pattern that matched a clock time or a version label would fail every
future branch for no reason. A negative `line` is constructed rather than copied, since the
point of it is a shape the repository must never start carrying.
A `lineCases` positive is copied verbatim where a real citation has that shape, and constructed
where none does, with the `why` saying which. Constructed is the better of the two and the one
to reach for when both are open: a case copied from the tree breaks when that line is corrected,
which is how the comma-list case came to carry a citation this very branch was fixing.

cases.why: positive: internal spec under notes/, cited as a repo-root path, never tracked
positive: a lost document cited with no directory segment at all, so the extractor must not require a slash
positive: build-time generated NOTICE written one level above the citing workflow, unresolvable from any rule
cases.line: run: cargo about generate -m Cargo.toml about.hbs > ../NOTICE-rust.md

cases.why: positive: a table row naming artefacts of a sibling repository outside kuma; docs-relative must not rescue it
positive: same table, the row the strategy code actually cites as its evidence
positive trap: docs pages named by filename only in changelog prose. docs/en/faq.md and docs/ko/faq.md are tracked, yet neither faq.md nor docs/faq.md is, so every one of these stays unresolved
cases.line: - `~/.kuro/` corrected to `~/.kuma/kuro/` across `docs/en/` and `docs/ko/`, 22 occurrences in 14 files: `configuration.md`, `contributing.md`, `custom-polymerase-editor.md`, `faq.md`, `troubleshooting.md`, `uniprot-and-alphafold.md`, `workspace-save-load.md`.

cases.why: positive trap: a zip member name inside a test literal. The extractor cannot tell it from a citation, so the allowlist is what absorbs it
positive trap: a Korean filename truncates to its ASCII tail, so the extracted reference is a fragment rather than the real name
cases.line: """Materialize the on-disk test fixtures described in 030_테스트_fixture.md.

cases.why: negative discriminator: mkdocs nav is written against docs_dir. Citing-file-relative gives kuro/01-load.md at the repo root and fails; only the docs-relative rule resolves it
negative: exclude_docs entry, a bare filename that only the docs-relative rule can resolve
negative: bare index.md in nav. Exact and citing-file-relative both miss at the repo root, docs-relative hits docs/index.md
negative discriminator in the other direction: citing-file-relative resolves docs/mame/04-activity.md while docs-relative would look for docs/04-activity.md and fail
negative: ../README.md from docs/README.md walks up to the tracked root README
cases.line: Both tabs share a project workspace; a hidden `__kuma_meta__` sheet in every Kuro xlsx export lets Mame auto-match sequencing reads back to the originating project weeks later. See the [project README](../README.md) for installation and architecture.

cases.why: negative: the link label is a real reference and must survive, while the .md inside the https target must not be extracted
negative: a bare external URL whose path ends in .md must produce no reference at all
negative: two tracked root files on one line, both resolved by exact match
negative: notes/ is gitignored but a handful of files under it are force-added and tracked, so a notes/ citation is not automatically unresolved
cases.line: ``notes/perf/memory-bound.md`` was taken at 512 / 32, so a formula that does

cases.why: negative: a line about markdown that contains no reference; the extractor must stay quiet
negative: a user-guide nav entry names an in-app help page that docs/site/help_pages.py pulls from docs/help/en at build time

lineCases.why: positive, constructed: a full repository path with a comma list that mixes a single line and a range, which must come back as one citation rather than four. Constructed on purpose. The real citation this was copied from has since become a symbol name, and while it stood in the tree a comment added above it moved every number in it, which is the drift the ratchet exists to make visible

positive: a full path whose directory names no tracked file, copied from a comment that says ingest/ where the tracked file is io/. The final segment is unique, so a basename fallback would call this frozen and the wrong directory would never be reported. A citation that spells out directories claims a location, and a claim nothing satisfies is unresolved

positive trap: an expected lint message inside a test assertion, not a comment and not a citation. Nothing in the extractor can tell the two apart, and the path is invented for the fixture, so this arrives as unresolved and the ledger's hand-written test-literal category is what absorbs it

positive: a prose comment writing its comma list with a space after the comma, copied from src/lib/mame/fileExtensions.ts. The whole list must come back as one citation. Before the space was allowed the match stopped at the first comma and froze a truncated string, so the second position entered no ledger and nobody owed it anything
positive: a bare filename only one tracked file carries, so a reader can still tell which file is meant
positive: a bare filename two tracked files carry, so the line number does not say which one
positive: a path no tracked file can satisfy, which is the bucket that needs a hand-written reason
positive: a plain range, and a cited filename whose own name carries a dot, which the last path segment must accept
positive: markdown is not scanned as a source, but a comment may still cite a position inside a note, and that is the same debt
positive: a leading path segment that begins with a dot, as every workflow path does
positive: a Rust path with two single lines, from the one citing form that names a host file
negative: a URL carries a colon before a port and may end in a path that looks like a position. Scrubbing it first is what keeps a localhost example out of the ledger
lineCases.line: // mock server at http://localhost:8080/static/model.py:3 during development

lineCases.why: negative: a release label is a colon after digits and dots. Matching it would fail every branch that writes a changelog heading
lineCases.line: // v0.16.85: combination genotype labels and a plate filled by residue position

lineCases.why: negative: a wall-clock time is digits around a colon with no path in front
lineCases.line: # final_summary records 12:30 as the acquisition stop

lineCases.why: negative: prose that names a file and then a colon, with no position after it
lineCases.line: * Open validators.ts: the guard is near the bottom

lineCases.why: negative: a template that formats a position at runtime cites nothing, so freezing it would pin a string that names no file
negative: the form the convention asks for. A symbol name must not read as a position, or the ratchet would fail the very fix it exists to encourage

allowlistCases.why: negative: nothing is reported while each entry answers for a citation the scan could not resolve. Without this case a rule that always reports every entry would look correct
positive: the last citation to a lost document was removed, so its entry answers for nothing and must be reported
positive: the real case behind the stale category. The citation text still exists but was corrected to a tracked path, so the reference stops appearing among the unresolved and the entry is stranded
positive: more than one stranded entry, reported in sorted order rather than allowlist order so the output is stable across edits
negative: an empty allowlist strands nothing, even when the scan left references unresolved. Those are reported as unaccounted for by the other half of the check, not here
the line ratchet keys an entry by citing file and cited string joined with a tab, and reuses this same rule to report an entry nothing cites. A corrected citation must leave the ledger shorter
two files citing the same position are two entries. If the key were the cited string alone, the second file would pass on the first entry and the ratchet would leak
